title: On Friendship and Old Age
author: Cicero
public_title: Are you scared of ending up alone when you get old?
hook: You fear being alone when you get old.

sections.title: Story
sections.narration: You fear being alone when you get old. Cicero wrote that true friendship shields the soul. He said a close companion beats wealth or power. Cicero wrote, “Friendship is the only cure for old age’s loneliness.” The Harvard Study, begun 1938 in Cambridge, finds friends add about seven years. The result? A 2010 meta‑analysis by Julianne Holt‑Lunstad shows lacking friends raises death risk about 50 %. That pattern repeats worldwide, called the social buffering effect. Dan Buettner’s Blue Zones research in 2010s shows friends cut disease risk about 30 %. The WHO reported in 2021 that social isolation raises mortality risk similar to smoking. That's it. So why do we assume old age must be lonely? Because stories focus on loss, not on proven health data. Modern psychologists call this the longevity partnership principle. University of Oxford 2015 study found oxytocin spikes during shared laughter, boosting immunity. So next time you think retirement feels empty, nurture a friend. Remember Cicero’s advice that companionship is medicine. You fear being alone when you get old.
